target.title: fix(infra): add NaN guard for date parse in session cost usage
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: In `src/infra/session-cost-usage.ts`, the `loadSessionLogs()` function iterates over session transcript messages and parses their timestamps for use in session log responses. When `parsed.timestamp` exists as a string, the code calls `new Date(parsed.timestamp).getTime()` to convert it to a numeric Unix-epoch-milliseconds value. However, there is no `Number.isNaN()` guard on the parse result. If the timestamp string is unparseable, `new Date()` returns an invalid Date and `.getTime()` returns `NaN`. This NaN silently propagates into downstream log entries and through the gateway's `sessions.usage.logs` RPC response boundary.

**Solution**: Add a `Number.isNaN()` guard immediately after `new Date(parsed.timestamp).getTime()` with a fallback to `0` (Unix epoch), matching the default value. The existing `parseTimestamp` helper in the same module (line 867) already uses `Number.isNaN(parsed.valueOf())` for safe timestamp parsing, so this applies the same established pattern.

**What changed**: `src/infra/session-cost-usage.ts` — the `loadSessionLogs()` timestamp parse path (line 2733-2735). Changed from unbraced single-line `if` to braced multi-line guard per repo `curly` lint rule:

```typescript
timestamp = new Date(parsed.timestamp).getTime();
if (Number.isNaN(timestamp)) {
  timestamp = 0;
}
```

**What did NOT change**: The numeric timestamp path, the default zero initialization, all downstream log formatting, the public API of `loadSessionLogs()`. All valid timestamps continue to parse identically.

Fixes #99413

## Linked context

- **Related PRs**: #94096, #93903, #89448
- **In scope**: `loadSessionLogs()` top-level transcript timestamp string parse path at line 2731-2735
- **Out of scope**: Other `new Date()` call sites without NaN guards — candidates for separate follow-up PRs

## Root Cause

**Trigger condition**: A session transcript message has a `timestamp` field that is a string but not a valid date parseable by `new Date()`. The code handles "string" and "number" cases but not the "string that fails to parse" boundary case.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Unparseable timestamp strings in session transcript data no longer produce `NaN` in `loadSessionLogs()` output; they safely fall back to `0` (Unix epoch).
**Real environment tested**: Windows 10 LTSC 2019, Node.js v22.11.0, openclaw @ commit 367df9ec1e
**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `npx tsx evidence/pr-99418/verify-nan-guard.mjs` — standalone script that creates real session transcript JSONL files with malformed timestamps on disk and calls the actual `loadSessionLogs()` function (no vitest, no mock framework). Also `npx vitest run src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts -t "malformed"` for regression coverage.
**After-fix evidence**: L2 direct function call via npx tsx. Malformed "not-a-valid-date-string" → timestamp=0 (isFinite=true). Valid ISO-8601 "2026-02-21T17:47:00.000Z" → timestamp=1771696020000 (isFinite=true). Two entries returned by loadSessionLogs: Entry 0 malformed→0, Entry 1 valid→1771696020000. Full terminal output from npx tsx run: `Entries returned: 2 | Entry 0: role=user content="bad timestamp entry" timestamp=0 isFinite=true | Entry 1: role=assistant content="valid timestamp entry" timestamp=1771696020000 isFinite=true | Verification: Malformed→0 ✅ PASS, Valid→1771696020000 ✅ PASS`
**Observed result after the fix**: The `Number.isNaN()` guard at session-cost-usage.ts:2733 correctly intercepts `new Date("not-a-valid-date-string").getTime()` → NaN and resets it to 0. Previously this NaN would silently propagate through all downstream log entries and the gateway's `sessions.usage.logs` RPC boundary (NaN + 100 = NaN, JSON.stringify(NaN) = null). Now malformed timestamps safely fall back to Unix epoch 0, matching the default initialization value. Valid timestamps pass through the guard unchanged.
**What was not tested**: Full end-to-end gateway `sessions.usage.logs` RPC with corrupted transcript injected into running gateway. L2 evidence covers the complete changed code path (file read → timestamp parse → NaN guard → fallback) via direct function call with real file I/O.

## Tests and validation

Regression test added to `src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts`: creates session transcript JSONL files with malformed timestamps, exercises real `loadSessionLogs()`, asserts malformed timestamps default to 0 while valid timestamps parse correctly.

```bash
npx vitest run src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts -t "defaults timestamp"
```

```bash
pnpm tsgo:core
```

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible — guard only activates on NaN; valid timestamps produce identical values
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations — inline verification + dedicated regression test
- [x] I have updated relevant documentation — PR body includes before/after comparison
- [x] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary — N/A, zero breaking changes
- [x] Risk level: Low — defensive guard, fallback matches existing default, no API changes
- [x] Merge-risk: Low — the `Number.isNaN()` guard pattern already used in `parseTimestamp` (same file, line 867)

## Current review state

- [x] Self-review completed — code fix verified, regression test added
- [ ] At least one maintainer review
- [ ] All CI checks passed
